IIII.}}</noinclude>''charge of thee, that they preserue thee'': {{verse|chapter=4|verse=11}}† and that ''in their hands they shal beare thee vp, lest perhaps thou knocke thy foote against a stone''. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=12}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering said to him, It is said, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Deut. 6, 16.''}}* ''Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God''. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=13}}† And al the tentation being ended, the Deuil {{sup|‖}} departed from him vntil a time.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=14}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 4, 12. Mr. 1, 14.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ THE third part: of Christes manifesting him self by preaching and miracles, specially in Galilee.}}∷ And {{sc|Iesvs}} returned in the force of the spirit into Galilee, and the fame vvent forth through the vvhole countrie of him. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=15}}† And he taught in their synagogs, and vvas magnified of al. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=16}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 13, 54. Mr. 6, 1. Io. 4, 43.''}}* And he came to Nazareth vvhere he vvas brought vp: and he entred {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Our Sauiour vsed to preach in their Synagogues.}}∷ according to his custom on the Sabboth day into the synagogue: and he rose vp to reade. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=17}}† And the booke of Esay the Prophet vvas deliuered vnto him. And as he vnfolded the booke, he found the place vvhere it vvas vvritten, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=18}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 61, 1.''}}* ''The Spirit of the Lord vpon me, for vvhich he anointed me, to euangelize vnto the poore he sent me, to heale the contrite of hart'', {{verse|chapter=4|verse=19}}† ''to preach to the captiues remission, and sight to the blinde, to dimisse the bruised vnto remission, to preach the acceptable yere of the Lord, and the day of retribution''. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=20}}† And vvhen he had folded the booke, he rendred it to the minister, and sate dovvne. And the eies of al in the synagogue vvere bent vpon him. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=21}}† And he began to say vnto them: That this day is fulfilled this scripture in your eares. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=22}}† And al gaue testimomonie to him: and they {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ He had a maruelous grace, and an extraordinarie force in mouing the harts of his hearers.}}∷ marueled in the vvordes of grace that proceded from his mouth, and they said, Is not this Iosephs sonne? {{verse|chapter=4|verse=23}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpon Munday in the 3 vveeke of Lent.}}And he said to them, Certes you vvil say to me this similitude, ''Physicion, cure they self'': as great things as vve haue heard {{sup|‖}} done in Capharnaum, doe also here in thy countrie. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=24}}† And he said, Amen I say to you, that no Prophet is accepted in his ovvne countrie. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=25}}† In truth I say to you, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''3. Reg. 17, 9.''}}* there vvere many vvidovves in the daies of Elias in Israel, vvhen the heauen vvas shut three yeres and six moneths, vvhen there vvas a great famine made in the whole earth: {{verse|chapter=4|verse=26}}† and to none of them vvas Elias sent, but into Sarepta of Sidon, to a vvidovv vvoman. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=27}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''4. Reg. 5, 14.''}}* And there vvere many lepers in Israel vnder Elisæus the Prophet: and none of them vvas made cleane but Naaman the Syrian. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=28}}† And al in the synagogue vvere filled vvith anger, hearing these things. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=29}}† And they rose, and cast him out of the citie: and they brought him to the edge of the hil, vvherevpon their citie vvas built, that they might throvv him dovvne headlong. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=30}}† But he {{sup|‖}} passing through the middes of them, vvent his vvay.⊣<noinclude>{{rh|||And}}</noinclude>
